clue.text: Section of road unusable without first being fixed

indicators.note: the remaining letters are repaired, i.e. rearranged
UNUSABLE goes without its first letter

explanation.surface: A stretch of road that nobody can use until the repair crew has been.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter goes, leaving NUSABLE; 'being' just links the letters to their rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus lane is a section of road set aside for buses.

clue.text: Outlaw runs out of farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

explanation.surface: A fugitive bolting from a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as a noun, a bandit, but it is the verb: to ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when read as a verb: to forbid by law or decree.

clue.text: Slept after last of classes is missed

explanation.surface: A student dozing off after a class goes by unattended.
explanation.walkthrough: KIP is informal British for a sleep. 'Is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past tense: not attending something, whether by choice or not, means you missed it.

clue.text: Love superhero darning up masks

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer inside it
in a down clue, reading upward reverses the letters

explanation.surface: A caped hero patching the mask they wear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom, so the hidden EROD A is taken backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as a verb, the answer being a stronger, more worshipful kind of loving.

clue.text: Cast care not for performer

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, scattering the letters

explanation.surface: A director shrugs off one actor in favour of another when casting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' pulls toward theatre, which is where the answer lives, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactor is one who acts out a part: a performer.

clue.text: Shape aluminium on old anvil's centre

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A smith hammering aluminium into shape on an old anvil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shape' looks like the smith's verb; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one particular shape, an elongated egg-like outline.

clue.text: Work on regularly observed twitch of eye

parts.note: a tic is a habitual twitch

explanation.surface: Someone keeping watch on a colleague's recurring eye twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly observed' tempts you to take alternate letters; it just describes a tic, a twitch that keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an adjective, as in the optic nerve, so 'of eye' paraphrases it exactly.

clue.text: Disclosure of commercial assignment

explanation.surface: A leaked detail about an advertising contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' reads as an adjective qualifying 'assignment'; it is the noun, a TV advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a disclosure of something previously hidden.

clue.text: In burrow, start to obtain shade

explanation.surface: An animal underground trying to find some shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition setting the scene; it is simply the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a deep blue-violet colour, one shade among many.

clue.text: Season some sauerkraut? Um, no!

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone offered sauerkraut to season a dish and refusing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a verb, to add flavour to sauerkraut; it is the noun, a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the season between summer and winter, called fall in North America.

clue.text: App, number one in recruitment, draws in those learning trades

parts.note: to entice is to draw in

explanation.surface: A recruiting app that pulls in young people looking for a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws in' looks like the app's job description; it is ENTICES, the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprentices are people learning a trade under a skilled worker.

clue.text: Revolutionary mistaken in rash act

indicators.note: the letters are wrong as given and must be put right

explanation.surface: A rebel caught up in a reckless deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface already sounds like an anarchist's act, so the answer hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist is a revolutionary seeking to overthrow government.

clue.text: Poet turned to actress

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters of 'to' are read backwards

explanation.surface: A poet who switched careers and took up acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned to' reads as 'took up'; split it and 'to' is the fodder being turned. Brigitte Bardot is the French film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Bardot was a famous French actress.

clue.text: Quarrel with an unknown woman

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A spat with a woman nobody has met before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown woman' reads as one phrase; split it, since 'unknown' is Y and 'woman' is a first name, Tiffany.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Game chat

definitions.meaning: game here means animals hunted for food
British slang verb for talking on and on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a pastime; it is hunted animals. To rabbit (on) is British slang for chatting at length.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a hunted animal eaten as game; the other is a British slang verb, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.

clue.text: Induce good Parisian to pinch jewellery

explanation.surface: Tempting a nice Parisian into stealing jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' suggests theft, but here it means squeeze: B(RING)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal-verb synonym: causing a fever or labour to start, as a doctor might induce it.

clue.text: African lion mauled American

indicators.note: the letters are savaged out of order

explanation.surface: A lion attack on an American on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mauled' fits the lion so well it passes for part of the story rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a resident of one US state is necessarily an American.

clue.text: Left two notes on the counter for unsuccessful person

indicators.note: counter means against the direction, so the notes run backwards

parts.note: re and so are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a couple of banknotes on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests money on the counter; they are the musical syllables RE and SO, set down in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain paraphrase: someone who fails to win, or fails generally.

clue.text: Shelled crab vital for side dish

indicators.note: each word has its outer letters stripped, like a shell

explanation.surface: Crab meat, taken out of the shell, is essential to a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' fits crab naturally, but it applies to 'vital' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a South Asian yoghurt-and-cucumber accompaniment served alongside curries.

clue.text: Provided backing, established a carnival

parts.note: est. = established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A sponsor who funded and set up a carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided backing' reads as sponsorship; it is 'provided' (IF) turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym borrowed from Spanish: a public festival with parades and celebration.

clue.text: At home, kid told to eat

explanation.surface: A child at home being told to eat up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the verb, to joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal synonym: taking food or drink into the body, the clinical word for eating.

clue.text: Nearly all leaves in salad pitiful

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so those letters depart from the salad

explanation.surface: A pathetic salad that's almost all leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' pretends to be lettuce; it is the verb, departs. S(AL)AD minus AL is SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: pathetic or deplorable, as in 'a sad excuse for a meal'.

clue.text: Move around prison

definitions.meaning: to agitate, as with a spoon, or to begin moving

explanation.surface: An inmate shuffling round the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: STIR is old slang for prison, as in 'stir-crazy'.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb for mixing or rousing; the other is criminal slang for a jail.

clue.text: Longed to have new editor after period of time

indicators.note: 'after' means coming later in sequence, so the new editor's letters are written after the period

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone who wanted a fresh editor after a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longed to have' reads as one wish; 'to have' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past tense: wanted something intensely.
